messages:
Asha: Quick sync — StellarHealth private VPC onboarding. Staging env can't write audit logs to the customer's CMK in eu-west-1. App logs show `KMS: AccessDenied` on Encrypt. Anyone seen this exact pattern?
Liam_SE: 👋 yes — usually key policy doesn't allow the cross-account role or grants aren't set. Do we know if they're using a customer-managed key alias?
Asha: They asked us to use their CMK alias `alias/redwood-stellar-audit` in acct 123456789012. We didn't create the key; they own it.
Diego_NET: From the network side, endpoints to CloudWatch and S3 look fine. VPC endpoint to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com responds on tcp/443 from the private subnet.
Priya_Sec: Can you paste the exact error log and the role ARN the service assumes?
Asha: Error from the agent: 
```
2026-11-12T14:21:03Z | KMSError: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-stellar-service-role/i-0abcde is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```
Role: `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-stellar-service-role` (Redwood-managed role in customer account).
Priya_Sec: That looks like a key policy issue — the key likely only allows principals in the key account. Options: 1) customer updates key policy to allow the Redwood role ARN, or 2) customer issues a KMS grant for the role. Which do they prefer?
Asha: Customer prefers key policy edits so they retain audit trace in the key policy. I'll ask them to sign off.
Liam_SE: For a quick unblock, here's a minimal key policy snippet to propose to them:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodService",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-stellar-service-role" },
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Diego_NET: Also confirm there isn't an SCP or org-level deny for KMS actions. That can be a gotcha.
Asha: Customer says org SCPs are permissive for KMS.
Priya_Sec: Two housekeeping items: 1) Ensure CloudTrail logs kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey calls; 2) Add key ID + alias mapping to our onboarding checklist for audit evidence.
Asha: Adding to checklist now. Action items: 
- Asha: request signed approval from StellarHealth to update key policy (ETA: EOD)
- Liam_SE: draft policy + short rationale doc for customer and internal runbook (ETA: today 18:00)
- Priya_Sec: verify CloudTrail settings and produce a CloudFormation snippet to ensure kms events are captured (ETA: tomorrow)
- Diego_NET: run staging test after policy change and report results (ETA: after change applied)
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: `onboard/stellar/staging` at 2026-11-12T18:30Z — will post success/failure once done.
Asha: Thanks — please ping here when infra-bot reports. I'll coordinate signature with the customer legal/compliance contact.
Liam_SE: I'll include rollback steps in the doc (revert key policy + revoke grants).
Priya_Sec: Recommend we add a small 'proof of encrypt' test to the onboarding checklist: call kms:GenerateDataKey, store ciphertext in audit S3 bucket with tags `redwood:onboard=true`, verify CloudTrail entry.
Asha: Great — I'll capture customer feedback in the onboarding retro doc after go-live.
Diego_NET: One more fallback option — temporary routing of audit logs to a Redwood-managed CMK until customer's key is ready. Keep this as plan B.
Asha: Noted. Closing loop once we have the signed approval. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
